tasks.short: Teach health preservation and disease prevention

steps.what: Instruct individuals and groups on preserving health and preventing disease

tasks.design: The clinician gives instruction and responds to questions using approved material in {DOCS}. Material access supports the conversation without replacing explanation or checking understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice needs to fit the audience and its concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Vetted information supports instruction, but does not establish a saving in live teaching.
tasks.human_edge: The clinician hears concerns and makes information meaningful.
tasks.altitude: Instruction responsibility and contact time stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts provides guideline-based patient information. This supports access to vetted material, not a reduction in live instruction time.

assumptions: Boundary is instruction delivery, excluding separate material authoring and clinical diagnosis.
The clinician selects relevant material and assesses audience needs within s1; participants supply questions during instruction. No structured understanding score is assumed.
Use existing approved material first; native runtime earns no labour saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new information system or teaching process is added.
research_questions: Which explanations require individual clarification despite good written information?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Live instruction retains all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct medical research and test techniques

steps.what: Conduct medical research to investigate medications and develop or test medical techniques

tasks.design: The clinician conducts research under the authorised protocol stored in {DOCS} and uses existing research data systems {OTHER}. Scientific observations and interpretation remain human; no particular repetitive calculation is inferred from this broad task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scientific validity depends on trustworthy observations and a defensible method.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing data tools support research without replacing study judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing real effects from bias and understanding limits of evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The researcher recognises unsupported conclusions and unexpected findings.
tasks.altitude: Scientific responsibility and research effort stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: research conduct and interpretation remain human here; documentation-study results do not establish saved scientific work.

assumptions: Boundary is clinician study conduct and interpretation, excluding separately governed protocol approval, laboratory processing and publication administration.

The responsible study team supplies the authorised protocol before study activity. The clinician and study team produce observations during s1 before interpretation; no clean dataset or favourable result is assumed free.
OTHER means research data system. Test native data functions first; existing runtime earns no labour saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new automation is introduced.
research_questions: Which recurring data-handling activity has a measured baseline separate from scientific work?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Scientific work is unchanged and a clerical baseline is not invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify surgical suite, room and equipment requirements for scheduling
Schedule requested surgical suite activities into candidate room and equipment slots
Resolve conflicts and confirm the surgical suite schedule with responsible teams
Maintain use of operating, wash-up and waiting rooms and associated equipment

tasks.design: Configure native surgical-suite scheduling {OTHER} to propose slots from clinician-verified requirements and existing {CALENDAR} commitments. The anesthesiologist resolves conflicts, confirms the schedule and retains coordination of actual room and equipment use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated room and equipment slot reconciliation can require manual placement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scheduling can compare explicit windows and resource requirements without deciding clinical priority or readiness.
tasks.still_hard: Changing case duration, urgent cases and equipment that is unavailable despite a planned slot.
tasks.human_edge: The clinician balances patient and team needs and responds to actual conditions.
tasks.altitude: Less routine slot placement while suite coordination remains.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native room scheduling can propose slots from verified constraints; no digest case establishes local suite-scheduling savings or automatic clinical readiness.

assumptions: Boundary is the anesthesiologist's scheduling and suite-use coordination, excluding cleaning, sterilisation, equipment maintenance and other teams' execution.

OTHER means surgical-suite scheduling system. In s1 the anesthesiologist captures case ID, approved priority, requested room types, estimated duration, time window, required equipment, turnaround allowance, existing commitments and source versions; all capture and clarification remains in 25%.

Responsible suite and sterilisation staff supply existing availability and completion information under unchanged processes. The clinician checks its currency in s1 and actual conditions during s4. A candidate slot is not an equipment-ready or patient-ready decision; absent or stale availability sends the request to manual planning in s3.

Test native scheduling first; already automatic placement earns no new labour saving. Eight extra focal hours count rule changes and additional rescheduling; 5 other-role hours count suite-system owner resource mapping upkeep. No new staff availability reporting is assumed free.
unknowns: Actual scheduling duties and native functionality
Existing availability records and local confirmation rights
research_questions: Does slot configuration save hands-on time after requirement capture and rescheduling?
Can stale resource information remain clearly unconfirmed?

already_counted.description: Resource verification and structured scheduling capture

approvals.approved_version: Exact schedule, case and requirement versions, room/equipment assignments, times and team commitments checked in s3; changes void approval. It does not authorise clinical readiness or sterilisation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+20+35=80; gross 20%, net 12% after 8 focal upkeep. Range covers existing automated schedules with zero gain through 13 points of slot placement removed minus 8 upkeep. Requirements, confirmation and actual suite use remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Clinical instruction, research and suite judgement remain human; native scheduling offers limited placement savings.
reach: Coordinate resource provenance and handoffs with surgical-suite teams.
role.ambitious_version: More traceable suite schedules with physical readiness and live coordination fully counted.
